memory_update.text: Technology theme should be decomposed as AI/cloud demand pulling on physical semiconductor, packaging, optics, power, cooling, cybersecurity, and automation layers rather than as a single software or mega-cap semiconductor theme.

Semiconductor equipment subsystem suppliers are a priority underfollowed lane because they can be embedded inside many OEM tools while remaining less visible than ASML, Applied Materials, Lam Research, Tokyo Electron, or KLA.
Advanced packaging substrate materials, especially ABF/build-up film and high-end substrate capacity, should be tracked as a potential AI accelerator bottleneck.
High-purity quartz and crucible supply may be a speculative-shadow node where public-market exposure is indirect but systemic semiconductor dependency may be high.
AI optical connectivity should be mapped below transceiver assemblers into lasers, compound-semiconductor wafers, epitaxy capacity, and epitaxy tools.
Cloud security, identity, observability, and automation are plausible second-order beneficiaries but require Layer 1B evidence collection before ticker-level inclusion.

summary: Layer 1A decomposition frames Technology as a physical-and-digital infrastructure buildout rather than a single AI or software trade. The strongest discovery paths are likely below obvious mega-cap demand owners: semiconductor subsystem suppliers, advanced packaging materials, AI optical-connectivity toolchains, data-center power/cooling infrastructure, cybersecurity/automation control layers, and niche software/data plumbing that benefits from cloud and AI complexity. Current external context most strongly supports semiconductor supply-chain chokepoints around fab subsystems, high-purity quartz, ABF/build-up film and substrates, and compound-semiconductor epitaxy tools. Cybersecurity and automation are included as important discovery lanes but require fresh source work in Layer 1B before company-level claims.

Semiconductor capacity expansion and technology migration increasing dependence on specialized subsystems, materials, metrology, vacuum, power delivery, and process-control suppliers.

Manufacturing reshoring and geopolitical supply-chain scrutiny raising the value of qualified suppliers, regulated components, export-compliant tools, and localized infrastructure.

underfollowed_supply_chain: Semiconductor subsystem suppliers: vacuum, RF power, gas flow, process control, metrology, motion control, and specialty plating chemistry.
Advanced packaging materials and substrate enablers: ABF/build-up film, high-end IC substrates, plating tools, test sockets, thermal interface materials, and inspection.
High-purity mineral and quartz supply chain: quartz mining/refining, crucible manufacturers, silicon wafer inputs, and specialty ceramic components.
Optical-connectivity production chain: epitaxy tools, compound-semiconductor wafers, lasers, silicon photonics foundries, DSP/signal-integrity chips, and contract manufacturers.
Data-center electrical and thermal infrastructure: switchgear, transformers, busway, backup power, liquid cooling, pump/valve systems, controls, and grid interconnection services.

Cloud/cybersecurity/automation second-order software: identity governance, cloud security posture, data lineage, workload orchestration, observability, industrial automation software, and automated remediation.

theme_map.public_market_search_strategy: Use a two-lane funnel. Lane 1 maps reference leaders such as NVDA, AMD, AVGO, TSM, ASML, ANET, VRT, ETN, CEG, AMZN, MSFT, GOOGL, and META to understand where capex and demand originate. Lane 2 deliberately searches one or two layers below them for narrow suppliers with hidden customer dependency, qualification lock-in, low analyst mindshare, and $300M-$10B market caps where possible. Prioritize companies whose products are embedded in many OEM tools, materials stacks, optical components, power systems, cybersecurity workflows, or automation pipelines, but whose reported industry classification obscures the AI/cloud exposure.
supply_side_constraints: Long semiconductor equipment qualification cycles and high process risk make subsystem suppliers difficult to replace once designed into OEM tools.
Specialty materials such as high-purity quartz and ABF/build-up film appear highly concentrated and may be hidden bottlenecks below chip and substrate makers.
Advanced packaging substrate capacity and qualified substrate vendor concentration can constrain AI accelerator ramp schedules.
Optical-connectivity scaling depends on multiple chokepoints: lasers, silicon photonics, indium phosphide wafers, epitaxy capacity, and epitaxy tools.
Data-center power and cooling constraints may shift value from cloud operators to electrical equipment, thermal-management, grid-services, and component suppliers.
Cybersecurity and automation vendors may face less physical capacity constraint but can benefit from compliance pressure, cloud complexity, identity sprawl, and shortage of skilled security labor.
